key.name: pin-on-connect
key.description: After monitor hotplug, mode or layout changes, move windows back to their previous monitor and workspace. Restored frames are fitted into the current work area. A newly connected screen starts empty. Changes between mirrored and separate displays, or to the primary display without hotplug, establish a new baseline.

key.name: collect-on-disconnect
key.description: When a monitor is disconnected, collect its windows onto an empty workspace. Dynamic workspaces may append a new workspace; static workspaces reuse the active workspace if none is empty.

key.name: settle-delay-ms
key.summary: Settle delay after a monitor change
key.description: How long to wait after a monitor change before restoring window positions, giving mutter and other extensions time to finish their own relocation first. Raise this if another extension re-tiles windows after the restore.

key.name: max-restore-attempts
key.summary: How many convergence attempts to make
key.description: Mutter applies window moves asynchronously and can drop them, and dynamic-workspaces renumbers workspaces underneath a restore. Rather than assume one pass sticks, the restore re-checks every window against its target and re-applies what did not take, up to this many times. Raise it if the log reports giving up with windows still off target.

key.name: ignore-wm-classes
key.description: Escape hatch for applications that manage their own placement across monitor changes and should never be repositioned. Match against the window's WM_CLASS, e.g. ['Conky'].

key.name: debug-log
key.summary: Log window state to the journal
key.description: Log the tracked window state before and after each monitor change. Read with: journalctl --user -f -o cat | grep monitor-window-guard
